result.topic_en: The page ends a theorem on the impossibility of a quartic equation when p is a prime or a product of distinct primes, then solves two problems: making $(A+Bz)(a+bz+czz+dz^3)$ a square and making $(A+Bz+Czz)(a+bz+czz)$ a square, and shows how a second solution follows from a known one.
result.transcription:
218 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.

Theorema III. Si $p$ sit vel numerus primus, vel productum ex aliquot numeris primis diversis, tum vero numeri $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, etc. sint numeri ad $p$ primi, tum etiam haec aequatio semper est impossibilis:
$az^4 \pm bpy^4 \pm cppx^4 \pm dp^3v^4 = 0.$
Quia ob rationes superiores singuli numeri $z$, $y$, $x$, $v$, etc. non solum per $p$, sed per omnes potestates ipsius $p$ deberent esse divisibiles. Taliaque theoremata ad potestates altiores extendi possunt.
NB. Hae autem demonstrationes vim perderent suam, si esset $p=1$, quia omnes plane numeri divisibiles sunt per omnes potestates ipsius 1.
A. m. T. II. p. 10. 11.

53.

Problema. Reddere hanc formulam quadratum: $(A+Bz)(a+bz+czz+dz^3)$.
Solutio. Statuatur hoc quadratum $=(A+Bz)^2(p+qz)^2$ fietque
$\left.\begin{matrix}App\\-a\end{matrix}\right. \left.\begin{matrix}+2Apq\\+Bpp\\-b\end{matrix}\right\} z \left.\begin{matrix}+Aqq\\+2Bpq\\-c\end{matrix}\right\} zz \left.\begin{matrix}+Bqq\\-d\end{matrix}\right\} z^3 = 0,$
ubi duae solutiones sunt considerandae, primo si $pp=\frac{a}{A}$, sumatur $q=\frac{b-Bpp}{2Ap}$, tum erit $z=\frac{c-Aqq-2Bpq}{Bqq-d}$.
Altera solutio locum habet si $qq=\frac{d}{B}$; tum sumatur
$p=\frac{c-Aqq}{2Bq}$ eritque $z=\frac{a-App}{2Apq+Bpp-b}$.

Problema. Si proposita fuerit haec formula $(A+Bz+Czz)(a+bz+czz)$, eam reddere quadratum.
Solutio. Ponatur hoc quadratum $=pp(a+bz+czz)^2$ fietque
$A+Bz+Czz=ppa+ppbz+ppczz.$
Hic ergo si fuerit $pp=\frac{A}{a}$, statim fit $z=\frac{ppb-B}{C-cpp}$. Secundo si fuerit $pp=\frac{C}{c}$, erit $z=\frac{app-A}{B-bpp}$.
In genere autem si satisfaciat valor $z=f$, quo casu fit $pp=\frac{A+Bf+Cff}{a+bf+cff}$, tum semper alius valor potest inveniri; quoniam enim habetur haec aequatio quadratica
$zz-\frac{B-bpp}{C-cpp}z+\frac{A-app}{C-cpp}=0,$
eaque per hypothesin radicem habeat $z=f$; erit quoque $z=g$ existente
tam $f+g=\frac{bpp-B}{C-cpp}$ quam $fg=\frac{A-app}{C-cpp}$,
unde duplici modo alter valor $g$ reperitur. Hoc adhuc clarius ita ostendi potest. Cum esse debeat
$A+Bz+Czz=pp(a+bz+czz)$,
tum vero $A+Bf+Cff=kk(a+bf+cff)$,
semper alius valor pro $z$ assignari potest, existente pariter $p=k$. Dividatur prior aequatio per posteriorem fietque
$\frac{A+Bz+Czz}{A+Bf+Cff}=\frac{a+bz+czz}{a+bf+cff}$;
subtrahendo utrinque unitatem et dividendo per $z-f$ prodit
$\frac{B+C(z+f)}{A+Bf+Cff}=\frac{b+c(z+f)}{a+bf+cff}$,
unde $f$ facile definitur.

methods.what: Impossibility of a quartic equation with coefficients in increasing powers of p, by an infinite-descent divisibility argument
Set the product of a linear and a cubic factor equal to $(A+Bz)^2(p+qz)^2$ and kill the constant and $z$ terms to get a rational z
Alternative: kill the cubic and quadratic terms instead
Make a product of two quadratics a square by setting it equal to $pp$ times the square of the second factor
Special solutions when pp = A/a or pp = C/c
methods.quote: si fuerit $pp=\frac{A}{a}$, statim fit $z=\frac{ppb-B}{C-cpp}$. Secundo si fuerit $pp=\frac{C}{c}$, erit $z=\frac{app-A}{B-bpp}$

methods.what: A second solution g from a known solution f, via the sum and product of the roots of a quadratic (Vieta)
Divide the two equations, subtract one and divide by z−f to get a linear equation for the new root

$az^4 \pm bpy^4 \pm cppx^4 \pm dp^3v^4 = 0.$
items.english: Then this equation is also always impossible: $az^4 \pm bpy^4 \pm cppx^4 \pm dp^3v^4 = 0$.

items.quote: Taliaque theoremata ad potestates altiores extendi possunt.
items.english: And such theorems can be extended to higher powers.
To make this formula a square: $(A+Bz)(a+bz+czz+dz^3)$.

items.quote: Si proposita fuerit haec formula $(A+Bz+Czz)(a+bz+czz)$, eam reddere quadratum.
items.english: If this formula $(A+Bz+Czz)(a+bz+czz)$ is proposed, to make it a square.
